title: Rapid Taste-Aversion Learning by an Isolated Molluscan Central Nervous System

nodes.label: Pan troglodytes
nodes.description: The common chimpanzee species, a socially complex great ape native to tropical Africa and characterized by fission-fusion societies, extensive behavioral repertoires, and diverse forms of tool use.

nodes.label: Fission-fusion social system
nodes.description: A social system in which stable community membership coexists with flexible changes in subgroup composition, association, and spatial grouping.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee Party
nodes.description: A temporary subgroup of chimpanzees formed within a larger community during activities such as feeding, travel, resting, or social interaction.

nodes.label: Grooming
nodes.description: A social behavior in which chimpanzees manually inspect and clean the body surface of another individual and which can also function in affiliative relationships.

nodes.label: Social Bond
nodes.description: A relatively stable affiliative relationship between chimpanzees characterized by repeated association and grooming or other affiliative interactions.

nodes.label: Social network analysis
nodes.description: A quantitative approach used in the study to characterize chimpanzee social structures and relationships at individual and group levels.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee Community
nodes.description: A relatively stable social unit of chimpanzees occupying a shared home range and containing individuals that participate in the species' fission-fusion social system.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee Intentional Communication
nodes.description: Communication in which chimpanzees produce signals flexibly in contexts suggesting that they monitor and influence the attention or behavior of recipients.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee culture
nodes.description: Population-level behavioral variation interpreted as culturally transmitted when behaviors and associated knowledge are acquired and maintained through social learning.

nodes.label: Social learning
nodes.description: Learning influenced by observing or interacting with other individuals and considered important in the acquisition and maintenance of chimpanzee behavioral traditions.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee Gestural Communication
nodes.description: Communication using bodily movements, postures, or other intentional gestures during chimpanzee social interactions.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee vocal communication
nodes.description: Communication through vocal signals used by chimpanzees in social and ecological contexts.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee social bonding
nodes.description: Social bonding among chimpanzees expressed through patterns of association and affiliative relationships such as proximity and grooming.

nodes.label: Fission-Fusion Social Structure
nodes.description: A chimpanzee social organization in which a larger community repeatedly divides into temporary parties that change in composition over time.

nodes.label: Pan troglodytes verus
nodes.description: The western chimpanzee subspecies distributed across parts of West Africa and represented in research on behavior, ecology, genetics, and conservation.

nodes.label: Budongo Forest
nodes.description: A tropical forest in western Uganda supporting a long-term studied chimpanzee population, including the Sonso community.

nodes.label: Mahale Mountains National Park
nodes.description: A protected area on the eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika in Tanzania containing one of the longest-running field studies of wild chimpanzees.

nodes.label: Ngogo chimpanzee community
nodes.description: A large chimpanzee community in Kibale National Park that has been extensively studied for social organization, ranging, hunting, reproduction, and intergroup behavior.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee Grooming Partner Preference
nodes.description: Differential tendency of chimpanzees to groom particular social partners rather than grooming partners randomly.

nodes.label: Gorilla
nodes.description: A primate species compared with chimpanzees in relation to social organisation, group size, and social complexity.

nodes.label: Social brain hypothesis
nodes.description: Hypothesis proposing that the cognitive demands of complex social environments contributed to the evolution of larger primate brains, particularly expanded neocortex.

nodes.label: Social complexity
nodes.description: Complexity of social relationships and social structure within groups or communities, proposed as a focus for quantitative comparison across species and group sizes.

nodes.label: Group size
nodes.description: Number of individuals in a primate social group or chimpanzee community, used as a coarse proxy for social complexity.

nodes.label: Brain size
nodes.description: Relative brain size discussed in relation to primate group size and social cognition.

nodes.label: Neocortex size
nodes.description: Relative neocortex size or neocortex-to-brain ratio discussed as an indicator of cognitive capacity and its association with group size.

nodes.label: Chimpanzee community
nodes.description: Stable broader social unit of chimpanzees within which individuals associate in temporary parties.

nodes.label: Vocalisations
nodes.description: Vocal communication interactions considered as a possible component of social relationship maintenance and social network measurement.

nodes.label: Gestures
nodes.description: Gestural communication interactions considered as a possible component of social relationship maintenance and social network measurement.

nodes.label: Stable cohesive social groups
nodes.description: Social structure characterized by stable group membership and high spatial and temporal cohesion, contrasted with chimpanzee fission-fusion organisation.

nodes.label: Social differentiation
nodes.description: Flexible adjustment in the number of strong and weak social bonds maintained by primates, described as reducing the cognitive demands of managing social relationships.

nodes.label: Strong social bonds
nodes.description: Close social bonds that chimpanzees maintain in relatively small numbers, particularly in large groups.

nodes.label: Weak social bonds
nodes.description: Less strong social ties that chimpanzees maintain in larger numbers, especially in large groups.

nodes.label: Social relationship tracking
nodes.description: Retention and manipulation of information about social relationships, including indirect or third-party relationships.

nodes.label: Social knowledge
nodes.description: Information that primates retain and update about conspecifics and the outcomes of social interactions.

nodes.label: Social information updating
nodes.description: Integration of information to update knowledge about conspecifics and predict outcomes of social interactions.

nodes.label: Group size
nodes.description: The number of individuals in a chimpanzee social group or community, considered in comparisons of small, medium, and large groups.

nodes.label: Grooming
nodes.description: A behavioral interaction proposed for use in network analyses of chimpanzee social relationships.

nodes.label: Gestural communication
nodes.description: Communication through gestures, identified as a behavioral interaction for examining chimpanzee social relationships.

nodes.label: Vocal communication
nodes.description: Communication through vocalizations, identified as a behavioral interaction for examining chimpanzee social relationships.

nodes.label: Glucocorticoid levels
nodes.description: Hormone levels proposed as an objective biological measure of physiological well-being and social stress in chimpanzees.

nodes.label: Social stress
nodes.description: Stress associated with sociality, competition, and the demands of managing social relationships in groups.

nodes.label: Cognitive flexibility
nodes.description: The ability to flexibly adjust behavior according to the current social situation.

nodes.label: Social complexity
nodes.description: A social system in which individuals interact with many unrelated individuals across multiple social contexts.

nodes.label: Cultural complexity
nodes.description: A system containing a larger number of distinct behavioral forms specific to a social group.

nodes.label: Communication dialects
nodes.description: Culturally acquired differences in the form of the same communication signal type.

nodes.label: Vocal repertoire size
nodes.description: The size of an animal's vocal communication repertoire.

nodes.label: Social behavior
nodes.description: Behavioral organization and interaction among social individuals, including the regulation of social relationships.

nodes.label: Weighted directed social network
nodes.description: A social network in which ties have numerical weights reflecting interaction rate or frequency and may differ in direction between individuals.

nodes.label: Weighted ties
nodes.description: Network ties assigned numerical values based on the rate or frequency of behavioral interaction.

nodes.label: Directed ties
nodes.description: Network ties whose value may differ by direction between two individuals when interactions are asymmetric.

nodes.label: Grooming hand-clasp
nodes.description: A local custom of wild chimpanzees involving a hand-clasp during grooming, referenced for the Mahale Mountains, Tanzania.

nodes.label: Grooming-associated sounds
nodes.description: Sounds produced by chimpanzees in association with grooming, referenced in work on the Ngogo chimpanzee community.

nodes.label: Copulation calls
nodes.description: Vocalizations used by female chimpanzees during copulation and discussed in relation to social competition.
